idiom_name: facade class with constructor-injected collaborators (std::function for caller-supplied policy)
implementation_notes: The classic structure translates directly: a non-virtual (or virtual, only if clients must substitute it) facade class holds references to the fine-grained services and exposes one coarse method per use case; std::function replaces an abstract callback interface when the caller supplies policy, and std::optional/std::variant carry the coarse result without exposing domain entities. There is no container, so the composition root constructs the collaborators and passes them in - what replaces the classic form only partially is the DI framework of other ecosystems, which is why hand-wired constructor injection remains idiomatic. Keep the class form whenever the facade must own the dependency graph for many clients; for a facade with a single collaborator, a free function taking the collaborator by reference is the simpler cut.
pitfalls: Storing collaborators by value slices the services (the classic object-slicing trap); store references, std::reference_wrapper or pointers, and remember the facade's lifetime is then bound to theirs.
A std::function capturing a facade member by reference and outliving the facade dangles; prefer capturing by value or documenting the required lifetime.
A facade class declared in a public header drags the domain headers into every client; use forward declarations, an abstract interface, or pimpl when the facade is a published boundary.
